decisions.executionNote: Raise and advance right arm toward mouse with gradual downward pitch; left remains parked. Geometry estimated from head RGB.
Continue elbow-up approach, aligning right gripper above mouse and pitching downward before descent.
Descend slowly over mouse, completing near-vertical grasp orientation; keep jaws open until alignment is checked.
Correct mouse alignment from wrist view, then close right jaws. Retention remains unverified until lift.
Lift closed right gripper and begin a small lateral transfer to test mouse retention visually.
Mouse stayed on table. Reopen and shift grasp toward its center, then descend for a second attempt.
Lower grasp around mouse with a small forward correction, then close. Contact depth is uncertain.
Lift and shift slightly with jaws fully closed to check whether the mouse follows.
Reposition open jaws farther forward and lower around the mouse body; prior lifts did not retain it.
Mouse is now centered between open jaws in the wrist view. Close fully, pause, then lift vertically to check retention.
Mouse moved during closure but was not lifted. Recenter over its shifted body and grasp lower to reach its sides rather than the rounded top.
Mouse tipped sideways during closure. Use a slow lateral shepherding motion toward the nearby pad while monitoring contact.
Mouse is now upside down nearer the keyboard. Re-estimate its lower tabletop position and bring open jaws directly over it.
Correct toward the visible mouse body while easing upward from contact, close, then make a short retention-check lift.
Mouse appears between the jaws. Lift clear and begin transfer toward pad with the gripper kept fully closed.
Mouse slipped again. Correct tabletop-height estimate and approach its current location substantially lower with open jaws.
Ease off tabletop contact, shift jaws left and rearward to the mouse's latest RGB center, and close without further descent.
Maintain full closure while stationary to let the jaws settle around the centered mouse, then test with a very small lift.
Mouse remains centered between jaws in the wrist image. Lift and carry toward pad, keeping closure unchanged and verifying that it follows.
Mouse did not follow the lift. Reposition behind it for controlled tabletop sliding rather than another unstable lift.
Align the closed jaws behind the mouse and gently slide it forward, clearing the keyboard before moving toward the pad.
Correct the lateral offset: mouse lies left of the closed-jaw center. Reopen and center directly over it using its latest head projection.
Lift open fingers fully clear before any lateral correction; previous low repositioning pushed the mouse sideways instead of straddling it.
Descend vertically over the now-centered mouse with open jaws, avoiding lateral sweeping contact.
Finish a small vertical descent and hold steady with full closure around the mouse before testing retention.
Test retention with a slow vertical lift followed by a small rightward move, maintaining full closure.
Prior closure was above the mouse sides. Adjust forward while clear, then lower open jaws another two centimeters below the previous grasp height.
Close around the lower mouse sides, allow closure to settle, then perform only a small vertical retention test.
Carry the centered mouse toward the pad with a low, slow diagonal motion and full closure; verify whether it follows.
Mouse now visibly follows the gripper. Continue carrying it over the pad, compensating for its rearward offset from link6.
Lower and release mouse over pad, then lift clear. Begin the left arm's raised, elbow-up approach toward the alarm clock.
Mouse rests on the pad after release. Advance left gripper above clock and pitch downward; retract right clear of the pad.
Center the open left jaws over the clock with slow descent and near-vertical orientation. Continue returning the empty right arm.
Adjust left jaws slightly right and forward over the clock while lowering gently. Finish most of the right-arm return.
Use wrist view to center the clock between left jaws, lower slightly to its sides, then close. Right settles near origin.
Clock is between left jaws but tilted. Keep closure and lift gradually while retreating slightly from the far reach, checking retention.
Clock did not lift securely. Reopen above it, shift rearward to the body center, and descend with a more vertical grasp.
Clock shifted forward and is occluded. Raise slightly and advance open left jaws to regain a clear alignment view.
Clock is partly visible between the left fingers near the drawer. Close and test retention with a small upward, rearward move away from the reach limit.
Clock remains on the table. Advance open jaws to its actual body and lower below the top edge rather than closing above it.
Replan after IK interruption: retreat left wrist and tilt to a forward-reaching grasp, relieving the near-limit configuration instead of advancing vertically.
Previous retreat was rejected before motion. Use submillimeter retreat and very small pitch increments to preserve joint continuity near the limit.
Continue the safer slanted approach: retreat link6 while pitching fingers forward toward the clock, lowering toward its side surfaces.
Clock is visible high-left in the wrist view. Shift left and forward in small increments, lowering toward the body while preserving the slanted configuration.
Open fingers appear obstructed by the drawer edge. Narrow the aperture, ease slightly away from that edge and lower gently before closing on the clock.
Recenter slightly left and forward on the clock seen in the wrist view, using a limited aperture near the drawer wall; close after settling.
Drawer wall obstructs the side-to-side grasp. Lift away and rotate left gripper toward a front-to-back grasp to avoid that wall.
Complete the quarter-turn so jaws close front-to-back, advancing above the clock from its unobstructed right side.
Replan after continuity rejection: lower and retreat slightly to regain joint margin, with much smaller yaw increments.
Tilt the fingers forward toward the clock while keeping link6 back from the reach limit, and descend gently with front-to-back jaw alignment.
Clock is now visible beside the front-to-back jaws. Advance and lower a little to straddle its body, then close without sweeping sideways.
Closure missed the clock to the forward side. Reopen, lift slightly, and advance the front-to-back grasp center in small continuous steps.
Withdraw left from the obstructed clock while maintaining elbow-up continuity. Prepare the right arm for a low keyboard push; clock placement remains unresolved.
Bring closed grippers toward the keyboard's near corners, undoing left yaw gradually and keeping each arm on its own side.
Set both closed grippers behind the keyboard's near edge at pushing height, pulling the left hand back before the coordinated push.
Push keyboard diagonally forward-right toward its outline, advancing the right corner slightly farther to reduce its skew.
Keyboard rotated because the right contact was on its side. Lift both hands clear and reposition right behind the near-right corner for a correcting push.
Lower the right closed fingertips behind the keyboard's near-right corner; keep left clear so the next push can correct rotation.
Push the keyboard's near-right corner forward slowly to reduce its clockwise skew while left remains clear.
Continue the small right-corner push to straighten the keyboard, with a slight inward correction to maintain near-edge contact.
Release the constrained right contact and lift away. Bring left closed fingertips toward the keyboard's left edge for a rightward centering push.
Slide the keyboard rightward with the left closed fingertips while withdrawing the right gripper fully clear of its opposite edge.
The side push increased skew. Withdraw left and place right above the keyboard's lowest near corner for a direct forward corrective push.
Lower behind the near corner without lateral motion, then start a small forward push to straighten the keyboard.
Advance directly into the near keyboard corner with closed right fingertips to rotate it toward the frame; left stays clear.
Move the right contact toward the keyboard's outer near-right corner for stronger rotation correction. Bring open left gripper above the figurine in its own workspace.
Center left jaws over the figurine torso while right makes a gentle forward push at the keyboard's outer near corner.
Lift left fingers clear before centering farther left over the figurine. Withdraw right from the keyboard, which still needs alignment.
Figurine has settled on its back. Approach its waist from above with left jaws open, while returning the empty right arm toward origin.
